reading: The market RALLIED ~21% through the Czech coup + the March 1948 war scare + Marshall Plan tensions -- treating US-USSR war as low-probability (Marshall Plan recovery optimism dominated).
A shrug. The start of the blockade barely dented a market near its high.
A real decline, but it tracked the Nov-1948 NBER recession and the surprise Truman re-election (business feared his policies), NOT Berlin war fear.
The market was near its lows and did NOT rally on the lift -- it fell further to 13.55 by mid-June. Berlin's resolution produced nothing because Berlin was never what the market was pricing.
